alternative_queries: Empirical studies comparing pointwise binary cross-entropy with pairwise ranking losses, listwise learning-to-rank objectives, sampled-softmax, and differentiable nDCG or top-k surrogates for implicit-feedback recommender systems; evaluate GAUC and especially nDCG@5 using temporally ordered logged-impression data.

Learning-to-rank objectives for improving top-five recommendation quality under implicit feedback: compare BCE, BPR and other pairwise losses, listwise softmax or ListNet/ListMLE objectives, sampled-softmax, and differentiable ranking losses, with temporal train-validation-test splits and GAUC plus nDCG@5 evaluation.

Literature on optimizing nDCG@5 in industrial or large-scale implicit-feedback recommendation, focusing on changes to the training signal rather than feature or architecture expansion; include pointwise BCE baselines, pairwise and listwise losses, sampled negative or sampled-softmax training, and differentiable top-k ranking methods evaluated on logged impressions over time.

Methodological and empirical evidence for replacing pointwise binary cross-entropy with ranking-aware objectives in implicit-feedback recommenders when overall GAUC is moderate but nDCG@5 is the bottleneck; cover BPR-style pairwise learning, listwise ranking, softmax and sampled-softmax objectives, LambdaRank or LambdaLoss variants, and differentiable approximations to nDCG under temporal logged-impression evaluation.

Top-k ranking loss functions for recommendation from implicit logged interactions: papers comparing BCE against pairwise, listwise, sampled-softmax, and differentiable sorting or ranking objectives, reporting GAUC and nDCG@5, with attention to impression-time availability, leakage-safe temporal evaluation, negative sampling, and whether objective changes improve top-five ordering without adding outcome-derived features.
